outcome: One measured failure drives a bounded strategy improvement or an evidence-backed keep-baseline decision.
currentProblem: A self-improvement mechanism needs real failure evidence and held-out checks to avoid optimizing its own judge.
constraints: Research must compare reuse and the smallest existing-Core approach, inspect primary sources and pin selected versions before READY.
Future dependency plans are assumptions, not delivered truth; worker execution requires delivered dependencies and a current Jev-satisfied plan.
Real-provider and live-product evidence must be identified separately from deterministic mocks; no fabricated API runs, costs or judgments.
successCriteria: One candidate is linked to a real pilot failure and evaluated with fixed product semantics and resource limits.
Held-out evaluation supports PROMOTE or KEEP_BASELINE; acceptance changes and producer-authored success claims cannot decide promotion.
Existing attempts remain pinned, new attempts use a promoted strategy only after authorization, and regression can trigger supported rollback.
